title: The Air We Share
briefing: A stagnant weather system is trapping particulate pollution over homes and industrial yards. Small workshops contribute less individually but sit closer to housing, making a simple volume-based order contentious. AI recommendation: Temporarily halt the largest sources and protect repair exemptions. This prioritizes immediate safety under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Factory filtration can be improved within a day, but rushing installation may require interrupting water-treatment supply lines.
private_intelligence.community: Residents near small workshops report exposure not reflected in the citywide averages used by the restriction model.
private_intelligence.economy: A blanket industrial shutdown will also stop parts production for emergency vehicle repairs.
private_intelligence.safety: Outdoor workers face the highest immediate dose; masks help, but rest and filtered spaces matter more than a warning alone.

choices.title: Restrict Largest Emitters
choices.description: Temporarily halt the largest sources and protect repair exemptions.
choices.consequence: Total emissions fall quickly, but exemption disputes reduce trust and interrupted production costs jobs.

choices.title: Target Exposure Hotspots
choices.description: Fund filters and paid work pauses around measured hotspots.
choices.consequence: Local protection follows measured exposure and improves confidence, while inspection demands and subsidies reduce reserves.

choices.title: Keep Industry on Reduced Shifts
choices.description: Require staggered production and expand public exposure warnings.
choices.consequence: Reduced shifts preserve repair supply and local income, but prolonged exposure and slower equipment renewal retain health risks.
